$schema_comment: W1-DATA-17 — expand/contract DDL hazard gate. Files at or below baseline cutoffs are grandfathered. Newer migrations must be online-safe or listed under waivers with an approved maintenance window. Do not rewrite checksum-locked db/sql files already applied in environments — waive + follow-up expand/contract migrations instead.

baseline.reason: Cutover at W1-DATA-17 COMPLETE; historical corpus kept forward-policy only (see DATA_W1_DATA_17_TIMEOUTS.md).

waivers.reason: W1-DATA-08 authenticity remediation on live transcript_issuances: non-concurrent index + validating FK/CHECK applied in a controlled Wave-1 maintenance window. Checksum-locked; online rewrite would break schema_migrations digests. Follow-up expand/contract must use CONCURRENTLY / NOT VALID for any residual hot-path DDL.  W1-DATA-18: validates a constraint without lifting FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY. Under FORCE RLS the tenant policy applies to the table owner, so Postgres runs the validation scan under it, a migration session has no app.tenant_id bound, the scan sees zero rows, and VALIDATE CONSTRAINT reports success without comparing anything. Demonstrated while fixing 098: one planted orphan row and VALIDATE returned success. These files predate the rule and are checksum-locked, so they cannot be edited. Waived rather than fixed in place, on this evidence: a live scan of every validated single-column FK on a FORCE-RLS table, run as superuser with session_replication_role = replica so all rows were visible, found 0 violations. The constraints are therefore unproven rather than known-wrong. Remedy is a forward-only re-validation migration using the 100 pattern (lift FORCE, validate, restore, in one transaction), not an edit to these files.
waivers.maintenanceWindow: 2026-09-14 Wave-1 DATA-08 remediation (single-tenant staging + production maintenance)

W1-DATA-06 residual: 23 tenant-owned tables carried tenant_id as text and so could not hold a foreign key to tenants(id) at all -- Postgres rejects the constraint outright with 'Key columns tenant_id and id are of incompatible types: text and uuid'. There is no expression-based FK, so migrating the column to uuid is the only route to referential integrity, and ALTER COLUMN TYPE always rewrites the table under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE. No online variant exists; the alternative is leaving 23 tables permanently without a tenant FK. The 23 FKs are added NOT VALID and validated in a separate step so the scan is outside the rewrite's lock window. Validation runs with FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY lifted on both the child table and tenants, restored in the same transaction -- without that, VALIDATE either passes without reading any rows or fails claiming every tenant is absent. The file refuses to run at all if any table holds a non-uuid or orphan tenant_id, so it cannot destroy data or validate vacuously.
